title: fix(core): ValueDataSource reads a Date condition in an object $filter as implicit equality (objectui#10829)
body:
Fixes #10829
Clause-②: no — the value face stops dropping a `Date` constraint that `@objectstack/spec`'s `ACCEPTED_FILTER_COMPARAND_TYPES` accepts and the converter lowers to equality; no declared surface moves.

Implemented by the `os-dev` agent dispatched by the `domain:ui` seat 2 on claim `5859216449`, session `https://claude.ai/code/session_014mXUNuFomfj24w7s1pZzhN`. Base `d425b8c7fe`, head `bd71843968`.

## What changed

- `ValueDataSource.ts`, `matchesFilter`: a condition the spec's `isAcceptedFilterComparand` accepts no longer enters the operator-map branch. It takes the existing simple-equality branch (`value !== condition`), the same `===` the AST arm's `=` arm in `matchesComparisonNode` uses. No new comparison is written. The `zeroKeyConditionRefusal` JSDoc sentence that said a Date's constraint "still vanishes" now says the matcher reads it as implicit equality.
- Route choice (reported, not silent): the order named `instanceof Date`; the gate is the spec's `isAcceptedFilterComparand` instead. Its answer for an object-typed value is `value instanceof Date` in the installed spec 17.4.0, so the answer is the same today. It is also the predicate `convertFiltersToAST` lowers a Date through, so any object-typed value the converter lowers as a comparand is one this matcher reads as a comparand. None of them can reach the zero-operator loop.
- New pin file `ValueDataSource.dateComparand-10829.test.ts`. The objectui#10833 pin in `ValueDataSource.emptyOperatorMap-10817.test.ts` flips from rows `1, 2` to no rows, and its comment names this card.
- `packages/core/src/adapters/README.md`: the sentence "a `Date` lowers, so it reaches the matcher as before, where its constraint still vanishes (objectui#10829)" is corrected. A paragraph under "What `$filter` executes" states the Date reading and the identity caveat.
- `.changeset/10829-value-source-date-comparand.md` (`'@object-ui/core': patch`) is new. `.changeset/10817-value-source-empty-operator-map.md` gains one dated note in the objectui#10533 form (see Acceptance notes).

## H1: reproduced on base `d425b8c7fe` (throwaway probe, not committed)

The rows are `date` (the same instant, as a `Date`), `iso` (`'1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z'`), `ms` (`0`), `other` (`new Date(1000)`), `missing` (no `created`) and `b` (status `'b'`, same-instant Date).

| filter | path | base answer | head answer |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `{ status: 'a', created: new Date(0) }` | object | `date, iso, ms, other, missing`, 0 warnings | none, 0 warnings |
| `{ status: 'a' }` (control) | object | `date, iso, ms, other, missing` | same |
| `convertFiltersToAST` of the card filter | converter | `['and', ['status','=','a'], ['created','=', Date]]`, the leaf `instanceof Date` | same |
| that lowered AST as an array `$filter` | array | none, 0 warnings | none |
| `{ created: new Date(0) }` | object | all 6 rows | none |
| card filter over the objectui#10833 rows | object / array | `1, 2` / none | none / none |

The target the object arm has to match is the lowered array's answer: no rows.

## H2: the AST arm's Date comparison

`matchesComparisonNode`'s `=` arm is `value === target`, which is **identity**. It does no `getTime` and no ISO coercion. The constructor `structuredClone`s every row, so a stored Date is never the comparand's instance. That holds even when the row was built with the very same `Date` object: that probe answered none on the array arm.

| stored shape | `=` | `!=` | `in [Date]` | `>=` / `$gte` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| same instant as a `Date` | false | true | false | true |
| same instant, ISO string | false | true | false | false |
| same instant, epoch ms | false | true | false | true |
| a different instant (later) | false | true | false | true |
| missing | false | true | false | false |

The relational arms compare a Date through its number (valueOf), so `>=` and the less-or-equal arm both match the same-instant `Date` and `ms` rows while `=` matches neither. The AST arm is not changed (order); see Acceptance notes.

## H3: the object arm's reading

The object arm's operator answers on base already equal their AST twins, over the six rows. `$eq` gives none (as `=`). `$ne` gives all 6 (as `!=`). `$gt` gives `other`. `$gte` gives `date, ms, other, b`. `$lt` gives none. `$lte` gives `date, ms, b`. `$in: [Date]` gives none (as `in`). `$nin: [Date]` gives all 6. No sibling moves. Only the implicit-equality position the card names is changed, and the siblings are pinned as parity controls (§3).

Invalid Date: `toFilterNodeSafely({ status: 'a', created: new Date(NaN) })` gives `ok: true`, and the leaf is a `Date` whose time is `NaN`, so the converter LOWERS it rather than refusing it. The base object arm answered 5 rows and the lowered array none. The head object arm answers none, which matches.

## Pins, red on base and green on head, and the ablation

- New file: 20 tests. §1 has the converter fact, the card filter, the filter alone, and one case per stored shape. In each the object answer equals the lowered array's answer read live, plus the shared answer written as-is. §2 is the invalid Date. §3 holds the controls: `{ status: 'a' }`, a string equality, a number equality, and `$eq`/`$ne`/`$gt`/`$gte`/`$lt`/`$lte`/`$in` against their AST twins.
- **Red on base:** the tests at head and `ValueDataSource.ts` at the base blob `9f583180` (the mutation was trap-restored, and the restored blob equals HEAD `14cd84df` with `git diff HEAD` empty). The run gave `Tests 9 failed | 27 passed (36)`. The 9 are the seven §1 filter/shape cases, the §2 invalid-Date case and the flipped objectui#10833 pin. The base answer for the card filter was `date, iso, ms, other, missing`. The green ones are the two converter-fact cases (they check the premise, on the converter only) and every control.
- **Green on head** `bd71843968`: the two files gave 36 passed. `packages/core/src/adapters/` gave `Test Files 15 passed (15)` and `Tests 403 passed (403)`.
- **Ablation**, done with `ablation-replace.mjs --delete`. It removed only the `isAcceptedFilterComparand` gate line: the anchor went 1 to 0 and the blob `14cd84df` to `ef908598`. The restore gave blob equal to HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty. Over `packages/core/src/adapters/` the run gave `Tests 9 failed | 394 passed (403)`: the same 9 Date cases, and nothing else reddened. The predicted direction was red and the observed direction was red. The first attempt landed the mutation, but the vitest invocation guard refused overlapping path filters (objectui#7814), so that run measured nothing. It was re-run with the directory filter alone, and the numbers above come from that run, on head `bd71843968`.

## Acceptance notes

- **The AST arm's Date identity is recorded, not changed (order).** `=` / `!=` / `in` / `nin` compare a Date by identity, and rows are cloned, so no stored value equals a Date comparand, not even the same instant held as a `Date`. The relational arms meanwhile compare by number, so the same-instant `Date` row passes both `>=` and the less-or-equal arm but not `=`. Both arms now answer one row set, and that set is none. The filter that used to select every row its siblings allowed now fails closed. `@objectstack/spec`'s `FILTER_COMPARAND_TYPE_CASES` declines to rule on this: "A Date comparand must pass the door and execute everywhere; what it MATCHES against a stored text/date column legitimately differs per storage form (ADR-0053), so no row set is asserted here." It is not filed. No public door was measured, and no named producer of a `Date` comparand into this face was found: the dashboard date-range producer `buildFilterCondition` emits the bounds it is given, and `DateRangeValue` and the preset table type them as `string`, not `Date`.

The diff is 2 insertions and 0 deletions.
